discussion_comments.comment_body: Otherwise, this would break any sort of usecase where people are relying on array -> string coercion.
^ Would be good to have a test for this too.

It migh also be a good idea to cache `Array.isArray` in a module scope `const` to minimise `[[Get]]` lookups of a mutable property:
```suggestion
		if (ArrayIsArray(arguments_[0]) && ArrayIsArray(arguments_[0].raw)) {
```

- I added a small test to see if chalk correctly casts int and array to string. This revealed a previously existing bug: `chalk(["abc"])` threw an error. This should now be fixed by adding the suggestion on line 198  as well https://github.com/chalk/chalk/blob/26c73d2b80f06f5673a7bb44433f69316f229629/source/index.js#L198
- Caching Array.isArray is indeed faster. (from 24M ops/s to 25M ops/s for the first benchmark).

Why not that? Chalk requires a closing code regex for building the style. No sense in re-calculating it for every single color-convert model in the loop right after it since it's the same for all of them.

I mean, it's a little bit dangerous to assign to `ansiStyles` as it's a single-ton. So if someone uses `ansi-styles` another place, their instance will also be monkey-patched. Might be a non-issue in practise, but wanted to bring it up.
Chalk did it before in the loop above. We can change that, though - I'm not opposed.
Also, [it's not applied globally](https://github.com/chalk/ansi-styles/blob/master/index.js#L119-L122). We fixed that a while back :)

I agree that recreating the RegExp object each time is inefficient, although the interpreter would probably catch on and lift the object. Let me update the pull request regardless, as you're definitely right that it's cleaner.

What the `code.close.replace` call does is escape the `code.close` string for use in a RegExp. The outer `str.replace` then replaces all (escaped) instances of `code.close` with `code.open`.

Essentially it's just:

``` javascript
originalString.replace(code.close, code.open);
```

Except the `code.close` string is first escaped for use in a RegExp and then turned into a RegExp with the `g` flag.

See:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3446170/escape-string-for-use-in-javascript-regex

Note:
Looking back at my code, I definitely could've explained this better.

Ok, thanks for the explanation. Makes sense now.

Couldn't you precompute this though. Like `code.closeRe`.

I wonder if there's any way we can do it without having to do ugly string replacement. We have all the data upfront, so should be possible.

Ah, didn't see your inline comment response.

We could indeed precompute all closeRe's - let me do that.

I'm afraid there is no way to do this without string replacement. The source string being passed in, to be wrapped in colour codes, can simply already contain other colour codes. There's no way to predict this, and it's also not guaranteed to always be the last character, e.g. if there's a three levels deep nesting.
